versions.research_rationale: EO 11293 adds a single item (8), Commissioner, Federal Water Pollution Control Administration, Department of the Interior, to level V of EO 11248. The family trace shows two later events on that item before the 1973 revocation. EO 11587 (March 15, 1971) substitutes the words 'Commissioner, Water Quality Office, Environmental Protection Agency' for the original description, and EO 11604 (July 2, 1971) deletes item (8). Retitling the item as an office of a different agency shows that the administration had been renamed and transferred before March 1971. Held sources cannot settle whether that statutory reorganization abolished the Interior position, which would end this placement earlier, or carried it forward under the new title, so that the placement ran to the July 2, 1971 deletion. The OFR 'Revoked by EO 11708' disposition is only a formal later event; the whole-order end is left open. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. No human certification is asserted.

savings_residuals.reason: The order only placed, removed or renumbered positions in pay levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule under 5 U.S.C. 5317 (formerly sec. 303(f) of the 1964 Salary Reform Act). Removal of a placement operates prospectively; pay already received is a completed historical consequence, and no entitlement, transfer of functions or right is preserved. Neither the acting order nor EO 11708 contains a savings or incumbent-protection clause for this order's items. The only carve-out, EO 11708 sec. 3's exception for the positions listed in its sec. 2, does not cover them; EO 11768's incumbent clause (1974) concerns its own list.

savings_residuals.reason: The order only placed, removed or renumbered positions in pay levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule under 5 U.S.C. 5317 (formerly sec. 303(f) of the 1964 Salary Reform Act). Removal of a placement operates prospectively; pay already received is a completed historical consequence, and no entitlement, transfer of functions or right is preserved. Neither the acting order nor EO 11708 contains a savings or incumbent-protection clause for this order's items. The only carve-out, EO 11708 sec. 3's exception for the positions listed in its sec. 2, does not cover them; EO 11768's incumbent clause (1974) concerns its own list.

unresolved_material_gaps: Clause EO:11293#sec2-item8-level-V and whole_order_end: the first end falls between the 1970 statutory renaming and transfer of the Federal Water Pollution Control Administration and 1971-07-02 (EO 11604 deletion). Needs the 1970 statute and the text of Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1970 to decide whether the Interior commissioner position was abolished or continued under the EO 11587 title.
claim.research_rationale: EO 11293 adds a single item (8), Commissioner, Federal Water Pollution Control Administration, Department of the Interior, to level V of EO 11248. The family trace shows two later events on that item before the 1973 revocation. EO 11587 (March 15, 1971) substitutes the words 'Commissioner, Water Quality Office, Environmental Protection Agency' for the original description, and EO 11604 (July 2, 1971) deletes item (8). Retitling the item as an office of a different agency shows that the administration had been renamed and transferred before March 1971. Held sources cannot settle whether that statutory reorganization abolished the Interior position, which would end this placement earlier, or carried it forward under the new title, so that the placement ran to the July 2, 1971 deletion. The OFR 'Revoked by EO 11708' disposition is only a formal later event; the whole-order end is left open. Family method: the researcher read the saved official Federal Register OCR text layers (heading to FR Doc line) of this order, of EO 11248 and of all 40 orders that the OFR disposition notes and the 1989 Codification list as amending it, plus EO 11708, 11715, 11736 and 11768, and traced every item of EO 11248 sections 1 and 2 through each addition, deletion, word substitution and renumbering. EO 11708 sec. 3 (signed and filed March 23, 1973; no other effective date) revokes EO 11248 as amended, except for the eight positions listed in its section 2; none of them is a position whose placement this order's text still supplied. Where a later amender deletes an item and inserts another in its place, the earlier item's placement ends on that amender's effective date; the series' separate 'substituting for the words' formula is treated as a retitling that continues the item. Pure deletions, renumberings and effective-date provisions are one-time edits completed when the order took effect. The 5 U.S.C. 5315-5316 amendment notes for 1964-1973 record no statutory placement of the positions concerned. Abolition of a position by unpublished departmental action is outside the held sources and is a limitation of this bounded search. Page images were not viewed; quotations are exact from the saved OCR, including its recognition errors. No human certification is asserted.
